paragraphs: Reinforcement learning is often framed as a search for a policy that maximizes reward over time. Once a sufficiently good policy is found, that framing leaves room for learning to end. This paper develops a precise alternative for situations where continued adaptation is central to what makes an agent successful.

The authors introduce a mathematical language for describing and classifying agents through their implicit search processes. Within this language, a continual learning agent is one whose search continues indefinitely. They then define continual reinforcement learning as a setting in which every best-performing agent belongs to that category. The distinction connects ongoing learning to the requirements of the problem, rather than merely to how long training runs.

Two motivating examples show how traditional views of multi-task reinforcement learning and continual supervised learning fit as special cases. The contribution is a conceptual foundation: it makes previously intuitive commitments explicit and supplies a common way to discuss problems where learning must remain an ongoing activity.
neurips-2023-a-definition-of-continual-r.tldr: The paper defines continual reinforcement learning as settings where all best-performing agents must keep learning indefinitely.

paragraphs: This paper builds a vision model with two interacting branches to investigate the division between spatial processing and object recognition in human vision. Its input sampling creates complementary visual patterns inspired by retinal cells, while its two convolutional networks reflect the brain’s dorsal and ventral visual pathways.

WhereCNN uses a global view to learn spatial attention and guide eye movements. WhatCNN uses a local view to represent the object near the current fixation. Recurrent interaction between the branches lets the model accumulate a scene representation as its fixation moves. The architecture therefore connects decisions about where to look with representations of what is seen.

The researchers compared model activity with human brain activity during the same movie, assessing alignment through linear transformations. WhereCNN and WhatCNN preferentially matched dorsal and ventral pathways, respectively. In their model, differing learning objectives explained this separation more than retinal sampling differences or sensitivity to attention-driven eye movements. The authors consequently suggest that distinct processing goals may help explain biological pathway specialization; this remains an interpretation of model-based findings.
neurips-2023-a-dual-stream-neural-networ.tldr: A two-branch vision model suggests that different learning goals help explain the brain’s separation of spatial and object processing.

paragraphs: Spatiotemporal point processes describe discrete events occurring across space and time. Learning them requires integrating an event-intensity function over those dimensions, which can be computationally difficult. Existing approaches either restrict the function’s mathematical form or approximate the integral through random sampling, introducing numerical error.

Auto-STPP extends a dual-network integration approach from time alone to three-dimensional space-time modeling. A straightforward extension would impose excessive restrictions on the intensity and create difficult computations. The authors instead use ProdNet to express the integral network through products of simpler functions of individual variables. This decomposition makes the multivariate integration problem more manageable while supporting flexible intensity functions.

The paper proves consistency of Auto-STPP and evaluates it using synthetic and real-world benchmark data. Its reported advantage is recovering complex event-intensity patterns from irregular observations, especially when activity is concentrated sharply in particular regions of space and time. The contribution links a computational strategy for integration with improved recovery of the underlying event patterns in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2023-automatic-integration-for-s.tldr: Auto-STPP uses a decomposed integral network to learn flexible spatiotemporal event intensities with consistency guarantees.

paragraphs: Bi-level optimization couples an upper optimization problem to a lower one. Gradient-based methods must choose learning rates for both levels, and errors in estimating the upper-level gradient can make those choices delicate. This paper studies automatic step-size selection as a way to reduce tuning while retaining fast convergence.

The authors build on stochastic line search and stochastic Polyak step sizes. They first revisit these methods for single-level problems without the interpolation condition commonly assumed in earlier work. Their new variants are simpler to implement and fit within a shared family of envelope-type step-size rules. That common structure provides a route to extending both the algorithms and their convergence guarantees to bi-level problems.

Experiments evaluate versions based on SGD and Adam. The proposed methods find large learning rates with little tuning and converge faster than the corresponding conventional bi-level SGD or Adam methods requiring careful adjustment. The practical significance is coordinated adaptation of two interacting learning rates, supported by a framework that also connects the underlying single-level methods.
neurips-2023-bisls-sps-auto-tune-step-si.tldr: BiSLS/SPS automatically adapts both learning rates in bi-level optimization, reducing tuning and improving convergence in experiments.

paragraphs: Generating realistic examples does not by itself establish that a model can combine familiar concepts in unfamiliar ways. This paper investigates that compositional ability in conditional diffusion models through a controlled synthetic task. The researchers vary properties of the training data and measure generation of combinations outside the training distribution.

Their findings connect the order in which individual concepts and their combinations become learnable to the structure of the data-generating process. They also find that success on a combined task depends multiplicatively on success at its constituent tasks. This dependence can produce an apparently sudden improvement in composition, offering a partial explanation for emergent capabilities in generative models.

The study further finds that composing concepts appearing less frequently in training requires substantially more optimization steps than generating examples within the training distribution. Together, these results show how data structure, concept frequency, and training progress shape composition in the studied setting. The synthetic design supports a controlled explanation of these effects, rather than establishing that the same patterns govern every diffusion model.
neurips-2023-compositional-abilities-eme.tldr: A synthetic study links sudden compositional improvements in diffusion models to multiplicative dependence on constituent abilities.

paragraphs: Training under a tight memory budget can involve discarding intermediate tensors and recomputing them when needed. The paper identifies a weakness in existing approaches: they treat free memory at different addresses as interchangeable. Evicting scattered tensors may free enough memory in total while leaving fragmented space that does not all help allocate the next tensor.

Coop coordinates decisions about tensor allocation and recomputation. Its sliding-window eviction strategy removes tensors occupying contiguous memory so that the released space is immediately useful. It also introduces inexpensive tensor partitioning and recomputable in-place operations to improve allocation and further reduce recomputation costs. The central idea is that the location of freed memory matters alongside its amount.

Evaluation on eight representative deep neural networks reports up to twice the memory savings relative to the state-of-the-art baselines considered. The authors also report substantial reductions in computational overhead, search latency, and fragmentation. These results support treating memory layout and tensor eviction as a joint optimization problem when training with limited memory.
neurips-2023-coop-memory-is-not-a-commod.tldr: Coop jointly optimizes tensor allocation and recomputation to reduce memory fragmentation and training overhead.

paragraphs: Speaker recognition must identify a person from speech that also varies with what they say. Those two sources of variation are mixed in the signal, making it difficult to extract a representation focused on the speaker. This paper addresses that problem by explicitly modeling both speaker traits and changing speech content.

The proposed framework uses three Gaussian inference layers, each containing a learnable transition model that extracts distinct speech components. A strengthened transition model handles more complex speech dynamics. A self-supervision method then dynamically separates content using only speaker-identity labels, avoiding the need for additional labels describing what was spoken.

Experiments on VoxCeleb and SITW report average reductions of 9.56% in equal error rate and 8.24% in minimum detection cost. These are improvements in the reported recognition measures, rather than percentage-point claims. The authors also state that no additional model training or data is specifically needed. The practical contribution is a way to improve speaker representations by accounting for content variability within the recognition framework.
neurips-2023-disentangling-voice-and-con.tldr: A self-supervised disentanglement framework separates speaker traits from speech content and improves reported speaker-recognition measures.

paragraphs: Equivariance means that a model responds consistently to a specified transformation of its input. Building that behavior into every component of a large network can be difficult and computationally expensive. This paper studies adapting an existing pretrained model through a smaller canonicalization network that first places inputs into a standard form.

The authors find that canonicalization can make large pretrained networks equivariant, but its chosen orientations may differ from those encountered during pretraining. That mismatch can hurt predictions even when transformation consistency is achieved. They address it by using dataset-dependent prior information to guide the canonicalization function toward forms compatible with the model’s training distribution.

The resulting adaptation maintains model performance while substantially improving robustness to deterministic transformations such as rotations. The finding makes the relationship between canonicalization and pretraining central: choosing a consistent orientation also needs to respect what the predictor has learned. The authors suggest that this approach could support applications where relevant symmetries are known, rather than claiming benefits for every possible input transformation.
neurips-2023-equivariant-adaptation-of-l.tldr: Dataset-informed canonicalization makes large pretrained models equivariant while preserving performance and improving robustness to transformations.

paragraphs: Diffusion models can represent sequences of decisions, and reward functions can steer their generated trajectories toward better behavior. This paper asks whether a useful reward function can be recovered by comparing two such models: one representing lower-reward behavior and another representing higher-reward behavior.

The authors define a relative reward function between diffusion models and establish conditions for its existence and uniqueness. Their practical algorithm trains a neural reward function so that its gradients align with differences between the two models’ outputs. This uses the contrast between learned behaviors as a signal for the reward, connecting the approach to inverse reinforcement learning.

The method recovers correct reward functions in navigation environments, and using the learned rewards to guide a base model significantly improves performance on locomotion benchmarks. The authors also apply the idea to two large image-generation diffusion models. The extracted reward-like function assigns lower scores to harmful images. That demonstration extends the comparison-based approach beyond sequential decisions without establishing comprehensive detection of harmful imagery.
neurips-2023-extracting-reward-functions.tldr: Comparing diffusion models of lower- and higher-reward behavior enables learning reward functions that improve guided generation.

paragraphs: Neural networks combined with search can achieve strong reinforcement-learning results at substantial computational cost. Earlier work used path consistency to improve search efficiency in board games: designated evaluation values should agree along an optimal path. This paper extends that idea to environments where actions can produce nonzero immediate rewards.

The resulting method, GW-PCZero, generalizes PCZero and adds weights to reduce variance in value estimates arising from uncertain scouting. The paper also supplies theoretical support by proving that neural-guided Monte Carlo tree search finds an optimal solution under the path-consistency constraint. The guarantee depends on that constraint; it is not an unconditional statement about arbitrary learned search procedures.

On the Atari 100k benchmark covering 26 games, GW-PCZero reaches a mean score of 198% of human performance, compared with EfficientZero’s 194%. It uses only one quarter of EfficientZero’s computational resources in the reported comparison. These findings connect a reward-aware consistency rule and uncertainty weighting to improved computational efficiency while maintaining strong aggregate game performance.
neurips-2023-generalized-weighted-path-c.tldr: GW-PCZero extends path-consistent neural search to immediate rewards and reports strong Atari performance with substantially less computation.

paragraphs: Connecting written instructions to video requires identifying when each described step occurs. HT-Step provides labeled examples for studying that alignment in cooking videos. Each annotation pairs a time interval with a step category, linking a segment of observed activity to a step described in an instructional article.

The dataset contains 122,000 segment annotations across 20,000 narrated HowTo100M videos, covering approximately 2,300 hours. Its taxonomy contains 4,958 distinct steps automatically mined from wikiHow articles, along with rich descriptions. The authors report that it exceeds existing labeled step datasets in scale, task coverage, and the richness of its natural-language descriptions.

Using these annotations, the paper establishes a strongly supervised benchmark and evaluates baseline alignment methods. It also releases the annotations and specifies evaluation protocols and metrics so that subsequent methods can be assessed on a common task. The contribution is research infrastructure for procedural activity understanding: a substantial collection of timed step labels and a defined way to evaluate connections between instructions and video.
neurips-2023-ht-step-aligning-instructio.tldr: HT-Step supplies large-scale timed cooking-step annotations and a benchmark for aligning written instructions with videos.

paragraphs: Hypothesis selection asks which candidate probability distribution best matches observed data. This paper assumes that an unknown distribution is well approximated by one of n candidates and seeks a candidate whose total variation distance is nearly as small as possible. It studies how to do this when observations arrive in a stream and memory is limited.

The access model allows a specific operation on each observation: comparing the probability densities assigned to it by two candidate distributions. These PDF-comparison queries provide the evidence used for selection. The memory budget restricts how much information about earlier observations can be retained, making sample requirements and storage capacity directly connected.

The proposed algorithm achieves a nearly optimal tradeoff. For b bits of memory, with b roughly between log n and n, it uses s samples such that b times s is O(n log n). The result is optimal within an O(log n) factor throughout that range. It quantifies how additional observations can compensate for reduced memory under the stated streaming and query model.
neurips-2023-hypothesis-selection-with-m.tldr: The paper gives a streaming hypothesis-selection algorithm with a nearly optimal tradeoff between memory and sample requirements.

paragraphs: Causal disentanglement seeks hidden variables that explain observations through a causal model. A central question is identifiability: whether the available data distinguish the underlying explanation from alternatives. This paper studies unpaired observational and intervention data, where each intervention changes the mechanism governing one hidden causal variable.

The authors show that identifiability remains possible even when the causal variables are unobserved, provided a generalized faithfulness assumption holds. Their guarantee recovers the latent causal model up to an equivalence class, rather than uniquely resolving every aspect of it. In the infinite-data limit, the framework also permits prediction of effects from combinations of interventions that were not previously observed.

To implement the framework, the researchers develop an autoencoding variational Bayes algorithm and apply it to predicting combined perturbation effects in genomics. The contribution joins a conditional theoretical explanation of what hidden causal structure can be recovered with an algorithm for pursuing that recovery. The equivalence-class qualification and infinite-data setting are central to interpreting the strength of the guarantees.
neurips-2023-identifiability-guarantees-.tldr: Under generalized faithfulness, intervention data can identify hidden causal models up to equivalence and support unseen intervention combinations in the infinite-data limit.

paragraphs: Feature bagging combines predictors trained using different subsets or projections of input features to reduce prediction variance. This paper develops a theory for that strategy in noisy least-squares ridge ensembles. It derives learning curves and simplifies them for equicorrelated data, a special case with a shared correlation structure.

The analysis shows that feature subsampling moves the double-descent peak of a linear predictor. That observation motivates ensembles whose members use different numbers of feature dimensions. Varying those sizes provides a computationally efficient way to mitigate double descent, because the members do not all place their error peak at the same point.

The theory also compares a feature-subsampled ensemble with a single linear predictor. It identifies competing effects: subsampling can amplify noise, while combining predictors can reduce it. The authors find that these qualitative insights also apply to linear image classifiers using features from a modern deep learning model. The results explain both a reason to diversify feature counts and why ensembling benefits depend on the balance of noise effects.
neurips-2023-learning-curves-for-noisy-h.tldr: Learning-curve analysis shows how varying feature counts across ridge predictors can mitigate double descent while balancing competing noise effects.

paragraphs: Explanations are often generated after a model has learned its predictions. This paper instead considers prior knowledge about how a model should behave and turns that knowledge into constraints during learning. The goal is to understand when such explanation constraints can improve learning, as well as how to enforce them.

The theoretical framework considers model classes that satisfy the constraints in expectation over new data. For explanations expressed through gradient information, the authors characterize reductions in Rademacher complexity for linear models and two-layer neural networks. This measures how restricting acceptable behavior changes the flexibility of the model class and helps analyze the learning benefits of those restrictions.

The paper also develops an algorithm using a variational approximation. Across synthetic and real-world experiments, it achieves better performance and satisfies the explanation constraints more frequently than simpler augmented Lagrangian approaches. The expectation-based definition does not require every individual prediction to satisfy a constraint. Together, the theory and experiments connect prior explanations to both a more restricted learning problem and a practical training method.
neurips-2023-learning-with-explanation-c.tldr: The paper formalizes learning from prior explanation constraints and develops a variational method that improves performance and constraint satisfaction in experiments.

paragraphs: Efficient exploration depends on remembering where an agent has already been. A policy based only on the current state, or on a sequence of random moves, can miss that information. This paper introduces ηψ-Learning, which uses experience from the current episode when choosing the next exploratory action.

The method learns a policy that maximizes the entropy of the state-visitation distribution along a single trajectory. This objective favors spreading visits across states rather than concentrating them narrowly. Its focus on one trajectory makes the agent’s history within that trajectory directly relevant to deciding where to go next.

The authors combine variants of predecessor and successor representations to predict state-visitation entropy. These representations connect information about past and future visitation so that the exploration policy can be guided by its entropy objective. Experiments demonstrate strategic exploration and broad state coverage with limited samples. The contribution is an exploration method whose decisions account for accumulated episodic experience and whose objective explicitly rewards diversity of visited states.
neurips-2023-maximum-state-entropy-explo.tldr: ηψ-Learning uses episodic history and predecessor–successor representations to learn exploration policies that spread visits across states.

paragraphs: Neural MMO 2.0 is a research environment for reinforcement learning with many agents and many tasks. Its new task system expands the training settings available and makes generalization a central challenge. Agents can be evaluated on tasks and maps, and against opponents, that they did not encounter during training.

The environment uses procedurally generated maps. Its standard setting contains 128 agents, with support for between 1 and 1,024 overall. These capabilities bring task diversity and interaction with other agents into the same platform, providing a setting for studying behavior beyond a single fixed task or familiar group of opponents.

Version 2.0 is a complete rewrite that reports threefold higher performance, addressing simulation bottlenecks during online training. Improved compatibility also allows use of standard reinforcement-learning frameworks originally designed for simpler environments. The platform is freely available and open source with comprehensive documentation. Its contribution is an expanded and faster experimental environment; the abstract presents new evaluation challenges rather than a claim that agents have already solved them.
neurips-2023-neural-mmo-2-0-a-massively-.tldr: Neural MMO 2.0 provides a faster multi-agent, multi-task environment for testing generalization to unfamiliar tasks, maps, and opponents.

paragraphs: An equilibrium’s social welfare and the difficulty of computing it are usually separate concerns in game theory. This paper establishes a connection under a particular condition: when a smoothness argument guarantees approximately full efficiency, a family of no-regret learning algorithms can approach Nash equilibria. This enables fast computation through decentralized learning.

The authors use that connection to obtain convergence results for large games whose smoothness-based efficiency approaches full efficiency in the limit. Their framework covers seemingly different settings, including games with vanishing strategic sensitivity and two-player zero-sum games. It also identifies an equivalence between smoothness and the Minty property, connecting game-theoretic reasoning to an established optimization condition.

A further result concerns a family of no-regret dynamics using clairvoyant mirror descent. These dynamics achieve a welfare bound stronger than the smoothness framework’s bound while converging to the set of coarse correlated equilibria. The paper therefore supplies two related connections between welfare and learning dynamics, with distinct equilibrium conclusions. Its Nash-equilibrium result relies on the stated smoothness-based efficiency condition.
neurips-2023-on-the-interplay-between-so.tldr: Smoothness-based guarantees of near-full efficiency can also make Nash equilibria approachable through decentralized no-regret learning.

paragraphs: Graph contrastive learning trains node representations without labels by bringing positive pairs closer together and separating negative pairs. This paper investigates whether that training principle is followed equally well across nodes when the graph is augmented in different ways. Its experiments show that training is indeed uneven across nodes.

The authors introduce node compactness, a lower bound describing how well a node follows the contrastive principle over a range of augmentations. They derive this quantity through bound propagation. Looking at a bound across augmentations provides a way to distinguish nodes whose training behavior is more reliable from those whose behavior may violate the intended objective.

Their method, PrOvable Training, incorporates node compactness into binary cross-entropy as a regularizer. This guides learned representations toward better adherence to the contrastive principle. Experiments across several benchmarks show consistent improvements when POT is added to existing graph contrastive approaches. The contribution combines evidence of uneven node training, a theoretically derived diagnostic, and an add-on training objective that addresses the identified imbalance.
neurips-2023-provable-training-for-graph.tldr: POT uses a provable node-compactness bound to regularize uneven graph contrastive training and improve existing methods.

paragraphs: Language-model scaling usually increases both model size and the amount of training text. This paper studies what happens when the supply of distinct data is constrained. The researchers vary data repetition and computational budgets in experiments reaching nine billion parameters and 900 billion training tokens, examining how effectively repeated exposure substitutes for new data.

At a fixed compute budget, using repeated data for up to four epochs produces negligible changes in loss compared with using unique data in the studied regime. More repetition eventually makes additional computation yield no further value. The result gives a qualified case for data reuse while showing that its benefits do not continue indefinitely.

The authors propose and empirically validate a compute-optimal scaling law that accounts for diminishing returns from repeated tokens and excess parameters. They also investigate adding code data and removing commonly used data filters as responses to scarcity. Models and datasets from 400 training runs are released. The main contribution is an empirical framework for allocating computation when acquiring more distinct text is difficult.
neurips-2023-scaling-data-constrained-la.tldr: Experiments and a scaling law characterize when repeated training data remains useful and when extra computation stops paying off.

paragraphs: Linear inverse problems involve recovering an underlying signal from measurements that have altered or removed information. This paper presents a framework for solving such problems using pretrained latent diffusion models. Its distinction is operating with models that generate through a latent representation, while earlier posterior-sampling algorithms such as DPS and DDRM apply to pixel-space diffusion models.

The authors theoretically analyze their algorithm and prove sample recovery in a linear model setting. The analysis also provides an algorithmic insight that they extend to more general settings encountered in practice. These are separate levels of support: the recovery guarantee concerns the stated linear setting, while the broader application follows from extending the method’s insight.

Experiments cover random and block inpainting, denoising, deblurring, destriping, and super-resolution. Across the reported range of problems, the method outperforms previously proposed posterior-sampling algorithms. The contribution brings pretrained latent diffusion models into this recovery framework and combines a restricted theoretical guarantee with empirical evidence across several forms of image restoration.
neurips-2023-solving-linear-inverse-prob.tldr: The paper enables posterior sampling with latent diffusion models, proving recovery in a linear setting and reporting improvements across image-restoration tasks.

paragraphs: A neural solver trained to produce good solutions on average may not sufficiently optimize each new combinatorial problem. T2T addresses that mismatch by giving the learned model a supporting role in a search performed separately for each test instance. Training supplies knowledge of good solutions; testing uses that knowledge to improve a particular solution.

The framework learns a distribution of high-quality solutions through generative modeling, then conducts gradient-based search during testing. Its diffusion-based procedure adds noise to disrupt the local structure of a current solution and reconstructs a lower-cost one under guidance from the optimization objective. This creates a repeated improvement process connecting the learned distribution to instance-specific search.

Experiments on the Traveling Salesman Problem and Maximal Independent Set report average performance gains of 49.15% and 17.27%, respectively, over the previous state of the art. These are the paper’s reported performance gains, without a more specific metric interpretation supplied in the abstract. The results support combining generative learning with explicit test-time optimization for the evaluated problems.
neurips-2023-t2t-from-distribution-learn.tldr: T2T combines diffusion-based learning of good solutions with objective-guided search for each new combinatorial problem.

paragraphs: External tools can help language models answer questions requiring information or numerical reasoning beyond their internal capabilities. Evaluating that help is difficult when a model might already know the answer from training. ToolQA is designed to make assessment more specifically about using external tools to obtain and reason with information.

The dataset is produced through a scalable automated curation process and comes with 13 specialized tools for interacting with external knowledge. Its developers seek to minimize overlap with language-model pretraining data. That design choice aims to reduce the extent to which memorized answers can stand in for successful tool use; the abstract describes an effort to minimize overlap, not a guarantee of eliminating it.

The authors use ToolQA to diagnose existing tool-using language models, examining strengths, weaknesses, and possible improvements. They release the data and code to support further evaluation. The contribution is a benchmark designed around the distinction between internal knowledge and externally acquired information, together with tools and analysis for studying the reasoning needed to answer questions through those resources.
neurips-2023-toolqa-a-dataset-for-llm-qu.tldr: ToolQA evaluates language models’ external-tool reasoning with curated questions, 13 tools, and efforts to minimize pretraining-data overlap.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning requires both remembering useful observations and learning which actions influence later rewards. Both involve events separated in time, but they pose different problems. This paper investigates which of these abilities explains the strong performance of Transformer-based reinforcement-learning methods.

The authors formalize memory length and credit-assignment length, then build simple configurable tasks that measure them separately. This separation matters because success on a task involving a long history does not by itself show that a model can connect an earlier action to a distant reward. The tasks are designed to distinguish retaining information from learning delayed consequences.

In the experiments, Transformers improve memory capacity, including on tasks requiring observations from 1,500 steps earlier. They do not improve long-term credit assignment in the evaluated settings. The findings therefore attribute the observed advantage to stronger memory while identifying delayed credit assignment as an unresolved challenge. They also motivate benchmarks that vary the two demands separately so that improvements in one are not mistaken for improvements in both.
neurips-2023-when-do-transformers-shine-.tldr: Controlled tasks show that Transformers improve reinforcement-learning memory, including over 1,500 steps, without improving long-term credit assignment.

paragraphs: Visual relation detection identifies interactions or relationships between pairs of objects in an image. Using a vision-language model such as CLIP with simple category prompts can struggle to distinguish closely related interactions and overlook the objects’ spatial arrangement. RECODE addresses these weaknesses through more detailed descriptions of the visual evidence for each relation.

The method splits each relation category into subject, object, and spatial components. A large language model generates descriptive prompts for those components, providing complementary cues that distinguish similar categories from different perspectives. A further prompting procedure asks the language model to reason about suitable weights for combining the cues, allowing their contributions to vary.

Experiments on four visual-relation benchmarks support RECODE’s effectiveness and interpretability. Its central contribution is a way to translate relation categories into structured descriptions that better match the visual distinctions the task requires. The findings show the value of composite prompts and weighted cues for the evaluated zero-shot setting, where relation recognition draws on pretrained models rather than relying only on category names.
neurips-2023-zero-shot-visual-relation-d.tldr: RECODE improves zero-shot visual relation detection using language-model-generated subject, object, and spatial descriptions with weighted cue fusion.
